title: Judge Output (engage-lexicon)
description: Schema for the judge subagent's output in engage-lexicon. Required fields enforce decision-shaped output specialized for the legal domain: jurisdiction (propagated), weakeningEvidence (with authorityWeight + authorityType annotations on the cited authority), verdict, controlling-vs-persuasive distinction on every cited authority. Missing the controlling-vs-persuasive distinction blocks proposal generation (#202 AC6).

jurisdiction.description: The declared jurisdiction the judge reached its verdict under. Propagated from the gate; immutable input.

weakeningEvidence.description: Either a named citation from the against-advocate's report (index + one-line excerpt + authorityWeight + authorityType) that most weakened the for-case, OR the literal string 'none' with a justification. Missing field fails validation and blocks proposal generation. When a citation is named, the authorityWeight and authorityType MUST be present — these are the controlling-vs-persuasive distinction this skill enforces (#202 AC6).

excerpt.description: One-line summary of the specific piece of evidence that weakened the for-case.

authorityWeight.description: The controlling-vs-persuasive distinction on the cited authority. Required (#202 AC6). 'controlling' = binding on {jurisdiction}; 'persuasive' = informative but not binding.

authorityType.description: Authority type, drawn from citation-schema.json's authorityType enum. Required (#202 AC6).

value.description: Literal 'none' when no against-advocate citation meaningfully weakened the for-case under {jurisdiction}.

justification.description: Required non-empty rationale for recording 'none' — e.g., 'the against-advocate's citations were all persuasive-only and did not weaken the for-advocate's reliance on controlling Supreme Court authority.'

verdict.description: The judge's verdict on the claim under {jurisdiction}. endorse = the for-case held up; reject = the against-case succeeded; revise = neither survived intact, issue a revised claim. In survey mode, mapped semantically: endorse -> synthesis-recommended; revise -> synthesis-deferred; reject -> further-research-required (with surveyMode=true in envelope).

revisedClaim.description: Required when verdict === 'revise'. The revised claim statement the judge issues in place of the original, framed within {jurisdiction}.

flipConditions.description: When verdict is endorse or reject, names what would flip the verdict the other way under {jurisdiction}. When verdict is revise, names what would need to be true to reject the revised claim.

confidenceRationale.description: One-line rationale for the confidence level. When perAdvocateFabricationRisk has any true flag, this field MUST acknowledge it. When degradationFlags includes statutoryRecencyStale on a material citation, this field MUST acknowledge it.

degradationFlags.description: Collects any citationOverlap='unresolved', authorityHierarchyOverlap='unresolved', degradationEvidence='unverified', evidence-fabrication-risk, statutoryRecencyStale, statutoryRecencyUnverified, or recency-gate degradation warnings surfaced in earlier steps. Empty array when no degradation.

perAdvocateFabricationRisk.description: Per-advocate fabrication-risk flag propagated from Step 0 Return-side validation. Optional and defaulted false-false. When either flag is true, the judge MUST reference it in confidenceRationale.

surveyMode.description: Optional. Set true when the judge ran in --mode survey (refraction over N analytical perspectives instead of for/against/judge). In survey mode, verdict is semantically reframed (endorse=synthesis-recommended, revise=synthesis-deferred, reject=further-research-required) — see SKILL.md Step 5.

authority.description: Canonical citation form (e.g., '15 U.S.C. § 78j(b)', 'Basic Inc. v. Levinson, 485 U.S. 224 (1988)').

controllingAuthoritiesReferenced.description: Optional but recommended. Inventory of every authority the judge relied on in this output, each annotated with the controlling-vs-persuasive distinction. Useful for downstream proposal generation when the judge cited authorities beyond the named weakeningEvidence.
